item.title: WAInsight — open-source forensic analysis suite for WhatsApp Android databases
item.description:

Technical features: • FTS5 global search with forensic provenance tracking per message bubble • Hash-chained chain_of_custody.jsonl provides tamper-evident audit trail • Source databases opened read-only with SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY + immutable=1 guards • Handles 200K+ media files with sharded AVIF thumbnails and chunked metadata • Cross-contact analysis reveals shared groups, file hashes, and mention networks

item.title: AADGraphActivityLogs: How to Detect Legacy Azure AD Graph Attacks | Invictus Incident Response
item.description:
Microsoft releases AADGraphActivityLogs table, closing massive visibility gap in legacy Azure AD Graph API that attackers exploited for years with tools like ROADtools and AADInternals.
Security professionals finally have telemetry for the blind spot that threat actors have been abusing since 2019. While MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs covered the modern API since late 2023, the legacy graph.windows.net endpoint remained completely unmonitored - until now.
Key technical details: • Logs stored in AADGraphActivityLogs table with fields: CallerIpAddress, RequestUri, UserAgent, AppId, ServicePrincipalId, SignInActivityId • Schema similar to MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs but with naming differences (IpAddress vs CallerIpAddress) • SignInActivityId correlates to SigninLogs.UniqueTokenIdentifier (with padding difference) • SessionId enables cross-table correlation across SigninLogs, AADGraphActivityLogs, MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs
ROADrecon detection opportunities: • Behavioral fingerprinting: Single source hitting hardcoded endpoint sequence (/users, /tenantdetails, /groups, /applications, /serviceprincipals) • User-Agent detection: "Python/3.12 aiohttp/3.10.4" unless explicitly spoofed • Volume analysis: Tools like ROADrecon generate thousands of requests in seconds
Enable via Entra ID Diagnostic Settings. Hunt for high-volume GET requests to legacy endpoints with Python/aiohttp User-Agents or behavioral patterns matching reconnaissance tools.

item.title: The Danger of Multi-SSO AWS Cognito User Pools
item.description:
Doyensec reveals critical security flaws in multi-tenant AWS Cognito deployments where external IdPs can inject ghost identities, bypass authentication controls, and hijack domain routing through malicious SSO configurations.
Key vulnerabilities identified:
• JIT Ghost Identity Injection: PreSignUp_ExternalProvider trigger fires before user persistence, allowing attackers to create durable ghost accounts even when domain checks fail in PostConfirmation
• Trigger Source Confusion: Developers miss triggerSource values like PreSignUp_ExternalProvider vs InboundFederation_ExternalProvider, creating authentication bypass paths between first and subsequent logins
• Sub-Splitting Attacks: Federated username format `<ProviderName>_<sub>` vulnerable to parsing differentials when Lambda functions use `split("_")` with positional indices on attacker-controlled sub claims
• IdP Routing Hijacks: Platforms allowing self-service IdpIdentifier registration without domain ownership validation enable attackers to redirect authentication flows (e.g., claiming gmail.com)
• Provider Name Collision: Cognito accepts visually similar but byte-distinct provider names using homoglyphs, creating confusion in audit logs and potential identity conflicts
Implement security gates in PreSignUp with proper triggerSource branching. Use `split("_", 1)` for username parsing. Tool release: maSSO weaponized IdP for testing available on GitHub.
#DFIR_Radar | View on X: https://x.com/DFIR_Radar/status/2051633915685732817

item.title: [local] Linux Kernel proc_readdir_de() 6.18-rc5 - Local Privilege Escalation
item.description:
CVE-2025-40271 exploits Linux kernel proc_readdir_de() use-after-free in kernels ~3.14+ through 6.18-rc5. Race condition in /proc filesystem allows local privilege escalation via rb-tree traversal of freed proc entries.
Technical details: • remove_proc_entry() calls rb_erase() without RB_CLEAR_NODE(), leaving stale rb-tree links • Concurrent getdents64() on /proc/self/net/dev_snmp6/ can traverse freed proc_dir_entry structs • UAF triggered by racing directory reads against network device removal (veth deletion) • Freed 192-byte proc_dir_entry objects sprayed with msg_msg via msgsnd() for heap manipulation • Kernel heap pointer leaked through d_ino field enables KASLR bypass
Attack methodology: • Creates user namespace for CAP_NET_ADMIN capability • Populates /proc/self/net/dev_snmp6/ with veth pairs to create target proc entries • Races getdents64() against rapid veth deletion to trigger stale pointer dereference • Sprays kmalloc-192 cache with msg_msg to reclaim freed slots • Detects UAF via anomalous d_ino values (0xffff... kernel addresses)
Fixed in stable kernels 5.10.247, 6.1.159, 6.12.73, 6.18-rc6 via commit adding pde_erase() helper. Hunt for unusual d_ino patterns in getdents syscalls and monitor veth creation/deletion patterns.

item.title: Evaluating our Threat Hunting Detection Rules (+ KQL Query Evaluation)
item.description:
Security teams often create thousands of detection rules without proper lifecycle management, leading to alert fatigue and duplicated coverage. New DOVE model provides framework to evaluate detection overlap and value across four key dimensions.
Key methodology: • DOVE Model assesses Detection Type (IOC vs IOA behaviors), System Coverage (mainstream vs niche), Threat Recency (emerging vs known), and Source Provider (native vs custom) • IOC-based detections have shorter lifecycles and higher duplication risk compared to behavioral IOA detections • Mainstream technologies (Windows, M365, macOS) show higher overlap probability with built-in SIEM detections • Custom detections may become redundant as platforms evolve and add native coverage
KQL evaluation approach: • Query identifies alerts targeting same assets within 1-hour windows to detect potential overlap • Groups by DateHour, AccountUpn, DeviceName, RemoteIP, and other pivots • Filters for multiple detection sources including custom rules • Three scenarios: enrichment (valuable), chain identification (valuable), duplication (remove)
Run daily correlation queries to identify detection rules that evolved from useful signals into pure noise. Prioritize IOA-based detections over IOCs for longer-term value.

item.title: Copy Fail and the forensic blind spot hiding in Linux memory
item.description:

Key technical details: • 9-year-old optimization in algif_aead.c allows in-place AEAD operations, but authencesn implementation writes scratch data at offset assoclen+cryptlen into chained page cache pages • Attack path: AF_ALG socket → splice() target binary pages → sendmsg/recvmsg loop to inject shellcode into cached /usr/bin/su → execute for root shell • Affects kernels 4.14-7.0 (essentially all Linux since 2017), including LTS branches 6.12.x, 6.6.x, 5.15.x, 5.10.x • In containerized environments, page cache sharing enables container-to-host privilege escalation bypassing all pod security policies
DFIR implications: • File integrity monitors see clean disk while memory contains corrupted executable • Standard audit trails show normal su execution with no suspicious file writes • Syscall-level detection required: monitor AF_ALG SOCK_SEQPACKET socket creation outside disk-encryption tools (cryptsetup, veritysetup) • Post-incident forensics limited without real-time syscall capture of socket/splice/sendmsg operations
Deploy auditd rules for AF_ALG socket monitoring and Falco detection rules. Page cache corruption is invisible after reboot without preserved memory dumps.

item.title: What the March 2026 Threat Technique Catalog update means for your AWS environment
item.description:
AWS CIRT identifies three new attack patterns in March 2026 threat catalog update: Cognito refresh token abuse for persistent access, AMI deletion targeting recovery capabilities, and trust policy modifications for privilege escalation.
Key techniques documented:
• **T1098.A006 Cognito Refresh Token Abuse**: Attackers use `cognito-idp:GetTokensFromRefreshToken` to maintain parallel sessions up to 10 years with default token lifetimes. Legitimate user sessions continue normally, masking unauthorized access
• **T1485.A002 AMI Image Deletion**: `ec2:DeregisterImage` calls target disaster recovery capabilities by permanently removing golden images and recovery snapshots without Recycle Bin protections
• **T1098.003 Additional Cloud Roles**: `UpdateAssumeRolePolicy` API calls modify existing role trust policies to add external accounts, avoiding `iam:CreateRole` detection rules
• **Attack evolution**: Threat actors leverage legitimate AWS 🇺🇸 service behaviors instead of exploits, hiding malicious activity within normal operations and API call volumes
Monitor CloudTrail for refresh token calls from unexpected sources, AMI deregistration outside maintenance windows, and trust policy modifications to external accounts. Enable refresh token rotation and Recycle Bin retention rules for critical AMIs.
